title: SolarPunk Currency System Lab
thesis: Compress the currency-system path into one reproducible public-lab artifact without claiming mainnet adoption.

layers.name: Public lab primitive
layers.claim: Signed meter fixture data has produced a replay-protected SPK mint on Sepolia with public readback.

layers.name: Closed pilot surrogate
layers.claim: The same accepted bundle is treated as a named pilot stand-in to exercise the operating loop.
layers.blocker_to_upgrade: Governed attested-SPK redeploy plus one real meter or inverter export.

layers.name: Redeemable energy receipt surrogate
layers.claim: SPK is mapped to a bounded energy-credit equivalent at the observed energy price, with redemption represented as a ledger burn.
layers.blocker_to_upgrade: Legal/commercial redemption terms and a real operator obligation.

layers.name: Networked settlement asset surrogate
layers.claim: The minted SPK is circulated across a producer, gateway, maintenance provider, buyer, and merchant while preserving accounting conservation.

transactions.note: SPK minted from accepted surplus-energy attestation.
Producer pays the meter gateway for data service.
Producer pays maintenance provider in SPK.
Producer distributes SPK to a local buyer as an energy-credit settlement unit.
Buyer spends SPK with a local merchant.
Merchant settles an energy-credit invoice back to producer.
Buyer burns SPK against a lab-model energy-credit redemption.

claim_boundaries: Layers 2-4 are compressed lab models, not proof of real commercial adoption.
No token sale, mainnet readiness, yield, audit completion, or legal redemption claim is made.
The purpose is to test whether the currency-system logic is coherent enough to recruit real pilot evidence.
